newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK SOCIAL SECURITY SYSTEM NEEDS REFORM-BOGR GOV.
newsitem.headline: GREEK SOCIAL SECURITY SYSTEM NEEDS REFORM-BOGR GOV.

text.p: Bank of Greece governor Lucas Papademos warned that the country's social insurance system was in dire straits and the seven biggest pension funds in 1996 had a combined deficit of close to one trillion drachmas, a 25 percent rise over 1995.

"The ageing of the population will intensify the problem over the next few years," Lucas Papademos told Athens daily 'Ta Nea'. "Employees' contributions will be even less sufficient to enable the payment of pensions in the future than they are today."

The problem would require 'a significant period of time' to be dealt with and that the central bank was concerned about the impact of the pension funds' deficits on the budget deficit and debt, said Papademos.
Time was also needed to deal with the important problems of the gradual reduction of the debt and fiscal reform, he added.
"The government has committed itself to meeting budget targets and, subsequently, this commitment means that in event of significant divergence... it take structural measures," Papademos said.

He predicted that the banking system would see an increasing number of mergers and buyouts, and the state needed to reduce its stake in state-run banks but that it was not possible under current conditions for the state to completely excuse itself from the banking scene.
Papademos also sounded the alarm bell for banks' interest rates policy saying banks had to exercise sound judgement on rate cuts.

"Banks have to carefully evaluate their policies on interest rates for deposits and lending and not anticipate developments in inflation or to evaluate the reduction of inflationary pressures and reduce interest rates on deposits quicker than lending rates," he said.
Papademos said that the central bank planned to reduce required reserves in the near future. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
